sfcSequence.summary: Runs an ordered step/transition chart. Step setup executes on entry; the loop repeats while its following transition is not Boolean true. Parallel charts compile to cooperative VM workers.
inputs: Body: a valid chart of steps, transitions and matched branch/join blocks.
sfcSequence.returns: Command block; no reported value. Step flags and user actions change as the chart runs.
prerequisites: Use the shared JavaScript editor SFC overlay and a compatible MicroBlocks VM. These examples need no external hardware.
Create the named shared variables before choosing them in block menus. This is logical sequencing, not a certified safety controller.

examples.title: Build and inspect a small chart
examples.code:
Create shared variables Step1, Step2, Transition1, Transition2, Entries and Loops.
Under when started, add SFC sequence containing:
  step Step1 setup [change Entries by 1] loop [change Loops by 1]
  transition Transition1
  step Step2 setup [] loop []
  transition Transition2
Set Transition1 and Transition2 to Boolean false before starting.
examples.explanation: Start the chart, then set Transition1 true using the shared variable control. Step1 ends and Step2 becomes active. Set Transition2 true to finish.

notes: Examples describe visual blocks; bracketed bodies are command slots, not text to paste into a value slot.
Use distinct shared variables for step flags and transition conditions. Do not capture outer local variables in parallel workers.
Task and variable capacity are checked at compile time. A red stop may retain step flags; entering the sequence again resets them.

sfcStep.summary: Defines a named chart step, with setup actions performed once on entry and loop actions repeated while active.
inputs: Step: select an existing shared variable, used as its active flag.
Setup: commands run once on entry.
sfcStep.returns: Command block; no reported value. Step flags and user actions change as the chart runs.
prerequisites: Use the shared JavaScript editor SFC overlay and a compatible MicroBlocks VM. These examples need no external hardware.
Create the named shared variables before choosing them in block menus. This is logical sequencing, not a certified safety controller.

inputs: Transition: an existing shared Boolean variable controlled by another script or the variable control.
sfcTransition.returns: Command block; no reported value. Step flags and user actions change as the chart runs.
prerequisites: Use the shared JavaScript editor SFC overlay and a compatible MicroBlocks VM. These examples need no external hardware.
Create the named shared variables before choosing them in block menus. This is logical sequencing, not a certified safety controller.

sfcAnd.summary: Splits the chart into parallel branches running cooperatively. Use a matching join-all block after the branches.
inputs: Branches: two or more valid chart bodies; each begins with a step.
sfcAnd.returns: Command block; no reported value. Step flags and user actions change as the chart runs.
prerequisites: Use the shared JavaScript editor SFC overlay and a compatible MicroBlocks VM. These examples need no external hardware.
Create the named shared variables before choosing them in block menus. This is logical sequencing, not a certified safety controller.

examples.title: Build and inspect a small chart
examples.code:
Create shared step variables Source, B1, B2, After and Boolean transition variables Gate, Join, Done.
Inside SFC sequence:
  step Source setup [] loop []
  transition Gate
  parallel [step B1 setup [] loop []] [step B2 setup [] loop []]
  join all transition Join
  step After setup [] loop []
  transition Done
examples.explanation: Set Gate true to activate B1 and B2. Leave Join false to observe both active flags, then set Join true to reach After.

notes: Examples describe visual blocks; bracketed bodies are command slots, not text to paste into a value slot.
Use distinct shared variables for step flags and transition conditions. Do not capture outer local variables in parallel workers.
Task and variable capacity are checked at compile time. A red stop may retain step flags; entering the sequence again resets them.

inputs: Each branch has a shared Boolean guard and a chart body beginning with a step.
sfcOr.returns: Command block; no reported value. Step flags and user actions change as the chart runs.

examples.title: Build and inspect a small chart
examples.code:
Create shared steps Source, B1, B2, After and transitions Gate, Choice1, Choice2, Join, Done.
Inside SFC sequence:
  step Source setup [] loop []
  transition Gate
  OR transition Choice1 [step B1 setup [] loop []] transition Choice2 [step B2 setup [] loop []]
  merge transition Join
  step After setup [] loop []
  transition Done
examples.explanation: Set Choice1 false and Choice2 true, then set Gate true. B2 is selected. Set Join true to merge and enter After.

notes: Examples describe visual blocks; bracketed bodies are command slots, not text to paste into a value slot.
Use distinct shared variables for step flags and transition conditions. Do not capture outer local variables in parallel workers.
